title: Dittany: Contribution-Guided Repair Framework for MAS Applications
why: Locates unmet multi-agent task conditions and repairs actions or graph dependencies while retaining previously validated contributions.
note: 2026 preprint; evaluated across 30 applications and six MAS frameworks. Reported task accuracy is not external transaction integrity.

title: Evidence-Guided Recovery for AI Agents with Ambiguous Tool Outcomes and Partial Execution
why: Plans safe continuation after ambiguous tool outcomes using publicly supported effect states, provider contracts and independent replay certificates.
note: 2026 preprint; finite assignments and local-model comparisons. Certificates depend on declared provider capabilities; no general exactly-once guarantee.

title: Verify--Backtrack Loop: Structured Precondition Recovery for Long-Horizon Language Agents
why: Uses goal-stack verification and typed failure attribution to trigger explicit retry, subgoal updates or backtracking after unmet prerequisites.
note: 2026 preprint; AppWorld, ALFWorld and ScienceWorld experiments. Backtracking is an agent planning-state operation, not arbitrary external rollback.

title: AgentHeal: Evaluating Goal-Preserving Resource Recovery of Web Agents under Access Barriers
why: Benchmarks web-agent recovery from blocked links, authorization walls and rate limits while preserving the original authorized goal.
note: 2026 preprint; sandbox and real-website replay. Alternative resources must remain legitimate and policy-compliant; not generic transaction rollback.

title: ReplayRCA: Measuring Post-hoc Diagnosis and Live Oversight of Agent Failures by Counterfactual Replay
why: Restores failed LLM agent execution to the selected step and tests whether a proposed corrected action improves outcome against a placebo replay.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; deterministic OpsWorld evaluations and single-step intervention. Causal repair is measured against placebo, not external-world rollback.

title: Repairs for Whom? Evaluator-Executor Mismatch in Selecting Repairs for Failed LLM Agents
why: Tests whether candidate repairs selected by a different evaluator improve the deployed agent's own rollouts.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; tested on ALFWorld and WebShop. Reported 7B-versus-14B repair-ranking losses depend on the evaluator/executor pairing.

title: When to Intervene? An Empirical Study of Errors and Self-Recovery in LLM Agents
why: Analyzes natural self-recovery and predicts when external intervention is necessary.
note: Very recent preprint.

title: Permission to Retry: A Study of Authorization and Recovery in AI Agent Workflows
why: Examines whether recovering workflows still have authority to dispatch reconcile or retry an uncertain external effect.
note: 2026 preprint; 336 finite histories across native LangGraph and Temporal hosts; ancillary result files are linked from arXiv; no unrestricted production authorization guarantee.

title: CUA-Recovery: Benchmarking Error Recovery in Long-Horizon Computer-Use Agents
why: Benchmarks recognition and repair of inherited desktop errors over persistent workflows.
note: Paper reports 2250 test states.

title: Lost in Recovery: Demystifying Recovery Behavior of Computer-Use Agents via Goal-Oriented Action Replay
why: Introduces ReTrace and transition-consistent recovery scoring for computer-use agents restoring GUI state after controlled mistakes.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; goal-oriented action replay and injected GUI errors, not proof of remote system transaction rollback.

title: RITE: Evaluating End-to-End Resilience to Silent Tool Errors in E-Commerce Agentic Systems
why: Contrasts plausible incorrect tool values with correct values and explicit failures to measure recognition verification and end-task recovery.
note: 2026 preprint; 501 instances from 167 matched units and nine e-commerce workflows; domain-specific simulated tool behavior.

title: ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems
why: Learns when and how to amend in-progress multi-agent trajectories from execution-verified correction pairs.
note: 2026 preprint; author-reported repair results across selected frameworks and benchmarks, not independent external-effect verification.

title: Failure Recovery via Belief Updates and World Modeling for Long-Horizon Agents
why: BELIEFWEAVER retains evidence across failing attempts and checkpoints and uses belief updates plus prospective world modeling to guide repair.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; three terminal-agent benchmarks with author-reported gains; persistent reasoning state does not establish side-effect integrity.

title: UndoBench: Separating Task Competence from Recovery Capability in Tool-Using AI Agents
why: Measures conditional recovery separately from nominal task competence under phased enterprise write failures.
note: Preprint; 2,880 paired lost-acknowledgment trials are author-reported. Not evidence of production exactly-once guarantees.

title: Sentry: Learning to Recover from LLM Agent Failures at Test Time
why: Conditionally retrieves failure lessons and verifies repaired execution.
note: Check code release state.

title: AgentDebugX: An Open-Source Toolkit for Failure Observability, Attribution, and Recovery in LLM Agents
why: Links evidence-grounded failure diagnosis to bounded recovery proposals and controlled reruns.
note: EMNLP 2026 System Demonstrations; GAIA rerun results are author-reported and need a controlled environment.

title: From Credit Assignment to Repair: A Leakage-Controlled Diagnostic Study of Tool-Using Agents
why: Tests whether failure localization causes useful selective tool-agent repair and reports a reproducible negative result for its selected intervention gate.
note: REALM 2026 workshop; on tested tau2-bench tasks interventions rarely changed trajectories and did not improve binary reward. Negative result, not a recovery solution.

title: CUADebug: Diagnosing and Repairing Computer-Use Agent Failures
why: Inspects paired screenshots and actions for causal GUI errors and conditions re-execution on structured diagnosis.
note: EMNLP 2026 Findings; CUAErrorBench has 204 annotated failures; rerollout results depend on controlled restart settings.

title: Finding Where the Buck Stops: An Automated Failure Attribution-Based Reflection Framework for Multi-Agent Collaboration
why: DoCtOR targets reflection and correction at the decisive error agent and step instead of the entire team.
note: EMNLP 2026; reported improvements on question answering and web tasks, not generic multi-service rollback.

title: Causal Decomposition of LLM Agent Failure via Oracle-State Intervention
why: Tests whether replacing polluted context with oracle state actually rescues failed long-horizon agents.
note: REALM 2026 workshop; under 10% recovered after context replacement in stated WebArena default settings.

title: ParaRecover: A Process-Level Benchmark for Error Localization and Recovery in Parallel Tool-Use Agents
why: Evaluates cascading failure diagnosis and replanning across dependent parallel tool-call branches.
note: EMNLP 2026; 10,626 instances and 14 error types are author-reported; no global transaction guarantees.

title: PRFC: Learning Progressive Recovery from Function Calling Errors for Tool-Using LLMs
why: Trains successive corrective tool calls with progress-aware rewards after observed function-calling failures.
note: Findings of EMNLP 2026; multi-turn BFCL-v3 and three single-step tool tasks; improved call recovery does not certify external effects.

title: RecoverAgent: Intent-Preserving Recovery from Indirect Prompt Injection in Tool-using LLM Agents
why: Rewrites unsafe injected intermediate responses to resume permitted user goals after threat detection.
note: EMNLP 2026 Findings; tested on prompt-injection benchmarks. Safe continuation still requires tool outcome checks.

title: RESKILL: Explicit Failure Attribution and Structured Repair for Interactive Language Agents
why: Keeps structured failure hypotheses and retest feedback to choose and revise agent skill repairs.
note: EMNLP 2026; demonstrated on ALFWorld and TextCraft under fixed repair budgets, not real external writes.

title: ToolMisuseBench: An Offline Deterministic Benchmark for Tool Misuse and Recovery in Agentic Systems
why: Measures deterministic fault-conditioned recovery with typed recoverability and output-grounded scoring.
note: REALM 2026 workshop; seed-42 release includes 1,200 public-test tasks; offline evaluation.

title: Agent Error Dataset: Scaling 50,000 Error--Diagnosis Pairs for Failure Analysis and Error-Aware Post-Training
why: Pairs error diagnoses with candidate corrections and matched replay from common checkpoints when available.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; 50228 pairs and 3062 matched reruns are author-reported; resettable environments only.

title: Where Does Exactly-Once Live? Model, Harness, and Tool-Contract Effects on Duplicate Side Effects in LLM Agents
why: LIMBO injects late commits, duplicate delivery and partial batches; effect ledgers expose unsafe retries.
note: Preprint; 25,930 author-reported episodes. Tool-level idempotency contracts can be necessary where read-back cannot resolve in-flight writes.

title: Rollback the World, Keep the Reflection: Rollback-Induced Reflection for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
why: Couples controlled environment rollback with retained knowledge from the failed trajectory to guide subsequent agent execution.
note: 2026 preprint; evaluated in resettable interactive environments, not arbitrary third-party irreversible effects.

title: Locating Hidden Failures Makes Long-Horizon Agents More Reliable
why: Traverse labels mistakes and Scout predicts first-error locations.
note: Authors report 2518 trajectories and 6967 mistakes.

title: When Tool Calls Succeed but Workflows Fail: Anomalies at the Agent-Tool Boundary
why: Classifies external-effect anomalies that can survive tool success and derives reconciliation and transaction contract requirements at the agent-tool boundary.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint; effect-history model and MCP annotation audit over 98,291 tools, not an implemented general recovery engine.

title: AgentRewind: Recoverable Execution for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
why: Aligns agent-context and environment-state checkpoints for resumable execution.

title: Retry, Switch, or Abstain? Learning Strategy-Aware Tool-Use Policies via Controlled Error Injection
why: BENCH2ROBUST distinguishes retry switching tools and safe stopping under controlled failure solvability.
note: 2026 preprint; results reflect tested retail/tool benchmarks and do not guarantee real-world effect reversal.

title: From Faulty Memories to Corrected Actions: Dependency-Guided Rollback Repair for Memory-Augmented Agents
why: Tracks faulty memories through dependent actions, repairs affected persistent state and selectively replays work while preserving unaffected records.
note: 2026 preprint revised October; controlled and trajectory-derived tests; residual recurrence observed after selective replay.

title: Fail-Fast, Restart-Smart: Early Failure Prediction and Restart for SWE Agentic Tasks
why: Uses prefix-only early-failure monitoring and a fresh same-policy restart that can selectively reuse the interrupted code diff.
note: 2026 preprint; SWE-bench Verified reported token savings and recovery gains depend on chosen false-positive rate and coding-agent policies. A diff overlay is not universal side-effect rollback.

title: Real-Time Detection and Repair of LLM Agent Failures
why: Combines step telemetry and deterministic verification with repair experiments.

title: MemTX: Transactional Belief Commit for Stateful Agent Memory
why: Stages evidence-backed shared-memory writes and triggers cascading repair after a belief is retracted.
note: 2026 preprint; protocol invariants and tested environments do not imply universal compensation of irreversible actions.

title: AgentCheck: A Reproduce-Intervene-Mitigate Workbench for LLM Agents over MCP
why: Reproduces MCP tool faults and reruns agents under matched failures to test whether specific mitigations actually recover outcomes.
note: 2026 preprint; twelve injected fault types and five tested agents. Interpretive labels partly use LLM judgment; not broad production validation.

title: AIR: Improving Agent Safety through Incident Response
why: Introduces incident detection containment recovery and future guardrail synthesis inside agent execution.
note: ICML 2026; author-reported incident remediation results from three evaluated agent types, not independent production certification.

title: Robust Tool Use via Fission-GRPO: Learning to Recover from Execution Errors
why: Turns execution errors into on-policy training examples and resampled correction rollouts for multi-turn tool-call recovery.
note: ACL 2026 long paper; recovery rates are benchmark-specific; training benefit is not transaction-safe live replay.

title: Recovering Policy-Induced Errors: Benchmarking and Trajectory Synthesis for Robust GUI Agents
why: Introduces GUI-RobustEval with executable wrong-action recovery cases and RoTS recovery-trajectory synthesis.
note: ICML 2026; 1,216 test cases are author-reported. Controlled GUI evaluation is not arbitrary remote rollback.

title: Failure makes the agent stronger: Enhancing Accuracy through Structured Reflection for Reliable Tool Interactions
why: Benchmarks and trains explicit error diagnosis followed by an executable corrected tool call in failed multi-turn tool use.
note: Findings of ACL 2026; evaluated on BFCL v3 and Tool-Reflection-Bench; code release is not established by the proceedings text.

title: Mnemosyne: Agentic Transaction Processing for Validating and Repairing AI-generated Workflows
why: Uses deterministic admission, persistent transition logs, dependency-safe compensation and bounded reactive repair for proposed workflow changes.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint revised August; stated correctness holds relative to specified executable constraints and adapters, not all external systems.

title: Cordon: Semantic Transactions for Tool-Using LLM Agents
why: Stages agent tool effects in task-scoped semantic transactions with reversible shadow state, validation and recovery metadata.
note: 2026 preprint; staged effects and adapter boundaries only, not universal atomicity for all external systems.

title: From Failed Trajectories to Reliable LLM Agents: Diagnosing and Repairing Harness Flaws
why: Maps failed agent traces to faulty runtime-harness components and applies scoped patches with regression-aware validation.
note: 2026 arXiv preprint revised July; repairs recurrent harness flaws across evaluated benchmarks, rather than restoring a specific external effect.

title: When Tools Fail: Benchmarking Dynamic Replanning and Anomaly Recovery in LLM Agents
why: ToolMaze tests explicit or implicit transient or permanent tool perturbations.

title: DelAct: A Replayable Boundary Runtime for Auditable and Governed LLM Agent Workflows
why: Separates deliberation actuation and append-only logging for replay idempotent execution and compensation.
note: IEEE/ACM IWQoS 2026; demonstrated in a ticket/invoice workflow under selected faults, not universal rollback.

title: TraceFix: Repairing Agent Coordination Protocols with TLA+ Counterexamples
why: Repairs LLM-generated multi-agent coordination protocols using TLA+ counterexamples and enforces topology conformance at runtime.
note: ACM CAIS 2026 peer-reviewed; TLC checks bounded modeled protocol safety, not fidelity of model to deployed actions or universal liveness and external side effects.

title: Debugging the Debuggers: Failure-Anchored Structured Recovery for Software Engineering Agents
why: PROBE gates recovery guidance on structured telemetry and grounded diagnosis for subsequent repair attempts.
note: ASE 2026 paper; 257 initially unresolved cases and outcomes reported by authors; diagnosis does not itself guarantee recovery.

title: Robust Agent Compensation (RAC): Teaching AI Agents to Compensate
why: Studies log-based compensation layers that track agent effects and support corrective execution.
note: ACM CAIS 2026; evaluated compensation in selected LangChain and agent benchmarks. Handler correctness and remote provider semantics remain conditional.

title: Crab: A Semantics-Aware Checkpoint/Restore Runtime for Agent Sandboxes
why: Uses OS-effect inspection to make agent sandbox checkpointing more selective.

title: ACRFence: Preventing Semantic Rollback Attacks in Agent Checkpoint-Restore
why: Addresses semantically different tool requests after checkpoint restoration that can replay effects or resurrect expired authority.
note: 2026 preprint; proof-of-concept and proposed replay-or-fork mitigation; no blanket protection across external providers.

title: Wink: Recovering from Misbehaviors in Coding Agents
why: Monitors coding-agent drift, loops and tool failures and applies targeted runtime course-correction interventions.
note: 2026 preprint; author-reported production trajectory and intervention study; not general environment rollback.

title: Atomix: Timely, Transactional Tool Use for Reliable Agentic Workflows
why: Uses progress-aware resource frontiers to gate commits and distinguish bufferable reversible and irreversible effects.
note: Preprint; requires orchestrator/tool adapters. Authors do not claim distributed deployment or fully validated crash-safe exactly-once.

title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
why: Introduces MAST taxonomy and MAST-Data of 1600-plus annotated multi-agent traces to distinguish design misalignment and verification failures.
note: NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks Track; 14 failure modes from 150 manually studied traces. Diagnosis taxonomy informs intervention but does not directly recover committed state.

title: Where LLM Agents Fail and How They can Learn From Failures
why: Introduces AgentErrorTaxonomy and AgentErrorBench with root-cause targeted debugging feedback and iterative reruns.
note: 2025 preprint; separate original AgentDebug research from later AgentDebugX toolkit. Author-reported relative success gains on ALFWorld GAIA and WebShop do not certify external effects.

title: SagaLLM: Context Management, Validation, and Transaction Guarantees for Multi-Agent LLM Planning
why: Applies saga-style compensation persistent context and independent validation to multi-agent planning.
note: PVLDB 2025; compensating workflows relax ACID and cannot universally undo irreversible external effects.

title: Recovery-Bench: Evaluating Agentic Recovery from Mistakes
why: Evaluates agent recovery from prior failed trajectories and polluted context rather than clean starts.
note: OpenReview submission associated with NeurIPS 2025; publication or acceptance status not independently established; not external transaction recovery.
